answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post offers or attest to work. A verifier samples completed jobs, and if an identity’s claims fail, the protocol burns part of that stake and limits its influence. Creating a hundred Sybils then means tying up a hundred deposits, while one reusable identity can build a trusted thread of history. The wharf may welcome new agents, but the glacier of locked capital makes mass impersonation slow and costly.
